long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Mineola, New York, John “Hap” Fauth studied finance at Georgetown University, where he played football and captained the sailing team. After graduation he joined Citicorp, later opened the bank’s Minneapolis regional office, and became chief operating officer of Waterways Transportation. In 1982 he struck out independently, forming the investment bank that grew into the Churchill Companies.

Fauth built Churchill by buying, developing and holding businesses across industrial technology, agriculture distribution and commercial real estate, alongside investment funds for institutions and private clients. The firm remains family controlled and describes its approach as patient, operationally active and acquisition led. Beyond business, Fauth returned to competitive sailing after a long hiatus, won multiple world championships and co-founded American Magic in 2017 to challenge for the America’s Cup.

Fauth built Churchill by buying, developing and holding businesses across industrial technology, agriculture distribution and commercial real estate, alongside investment funds for institutions and private clients. The firm remains family controlled and describes its approach as patient, operationally active and acquisition led. Beyond business, Fauth returned to competitive sailing after a long hiatus, won multiple world championships and co-founded American Magic in 2017 to challenge for the America’s Cup.

Forbes published a direct 2005 feature item about Fauth, but exact-name and site-restricted searches found no dedicated profile page. Forbes profile status is therefore Not found rather than Verified.
